_readme: The Ninety-Nine — daily strip panels for The Daily Bread (SA-090/F-136). SUBJECT lines only; the founder-approved PREAMBLE and crop clause are assembled by scripts/imagery/build-strip-prompts.mjs, exactly as the series pipeline does. Panels are LANDSCAPE 3:2 only. Every generation MUST attach the four founder-approved style anchors as references: public/images/site/series/{prayer-of-jabez,he-cannot-deny-himself,looking-at-the-sun,the-harvest}.webp

_character_sheet.premise: The flock of Luke 15:4 — the ninety-nine left in the open country while the shepherd goes after the one. A strip about being the responsible ones nobody wrote a parable about. The register is dry, never mean; the joke is always on our own respectability, never on the lost.
_character_sheet.cast_rule: Sheep are drawn as simple high-contrast riso shapes: rounded woolly bodies in Ben-Day dot texture, dark slender legs and faces in dense flat ink, no human expressions — ATTITUDE COMES FROM POSE AND GROUPING ONLY (a turned back, a tilted head, a too-straight queue, one sheep standing apart). No eyes drawn larger than a dot. No anthropomorphic hands, clothes, or props held by sheep. They are sheep.

cast.The Flock: the ninety-nine as a mass — a dotted woolly bank filling part of the frame, reading as one body with many legs
cast.First Sheep: always at the front or facing the viewer's direction of reading; the self-appointed spokesman; identified by standing exactly where a responsible sheep should stand
cast.The Near One: one sheep always at the edge of the flock nearest the gap in the fold, half-turned toward the horizon; identified by separation distance, never by markings
cast.The Shepherd: appears ONLY as absence or at great distance — an empty crook leaning on the fold wall, a tiny robed figure on a far ridge line, per the PEOPLE clause. The strip is about the ones he left, so he is never the subject

_character_sheet.setting: one continuous location the reader learns: a dry-stone sheepfold in Judean hill country — low wall, one gap for a gate, a ridge line behind. Same fold every panel, drawn from different angles.
_character_sheet.caption_rule: Captions are typeset by the site under the panel, never drawn into the image (the preamble already forbids text in artwork). One dry line, written against the drawing.

subjects.strip-001-headcount: MID coverage, 45–60% ink: the dry-stone sheepfold interior at dusk, the flock of ninety-nine sheep packed as one dotted woolly bank across the lower half, every head down grazing except ONE sheep at front standing rigidly upright facing the viewer like a foreman taking attendance; the gate gap in the wall stands open and empty at the right edge; far ridge line quiet under faint tone. The count is the joke: the frame is FULL of sheep and still one short.
subjects.strip-002-the-gap: AIRY coverage, 25–40% ink: the fold wall running the width of the frame, the flock bunched hard against the LEFT end as one dotted mass, maximum distance from the open gate gap at the RIGHT; one sheep — the Near One — stands alone in the middle third, half-turned toward the gap, caught between the mass and the opening. Vast quiet cream sky above the wall.
subjects.strip-003-the-crook: AIRY coverage, 20–35% ink: the shepherd's crook leaning against the fold wall beside the open gap, abandoned mid-shift; the flock's dotted bank fills only the lower left corner, every sheep looking at the crook; long dusk shadow from the crook crossing the quiet cream foreground. He left the STAFF. It is fine. Everything is fine.
subjects.strip-004-single-file: MID coverage, 45–60% ink: the ninety-nine crossing the frame in an absurdly perfect single-file line along a hill path, evenly spaced, heads level, a queue of dotted woolly bodies from edge to edge; the line bends around a boulder rather than breaking step; far below in the valley, one tiny distant sheep visibly OFF the path on the wrong hillside. Order is its own reward.
subjects.strip-005-the-ridge: AIRY coverage, 25–40% ink: night tone, the flock bedded down as a single dotted bank inside the fold, all asleep except the Near One, upright at the wall, silhouetted head raised toward the far ridge line where a tiny robed figure with a crook descends carrying something across his shoulders; dense night tone above, quiet cream ground below. Nobody else stayed up.
subjects.strip-006-grass-audit: MID coverage, 50–65% ink: close on six sheep in a rough circle, all heads down on the SAME patch of grass, the patch nearly bare, while the entire rest of the frame is untouched pasture in quiet tone; one sheep's head raised mid-chew looking at the viewer. The good grass is where everyone already is.
subjects.strip-007-the-return: MID coverage, 45–60% ink: the fold at morning, gate gap at center, the returning shepherd a small robed figure in the gap setting down the found sheep; the ninety-nine arranged in a dense dotted semicircle facing the gate, front row rigidly straight — a welcoming committee that is also clearly a disciplinary hearing. First Sheep at dead center, most upright of all.
subjects.strip-008-one-missing-where: MID coverage, 40–55% ink: the flock as a broad dotted bank seen from behind, all ninety-nine heads turned to look at ONE conspicuously empty sheep-sized gap in their own middle — a hole of quiet cream in the woolly mass; the gate gap in the wall beyond stands open. They have only just noticed, and they are looking at the space instead of the hills.
subjects.strip-009-the-lamp: AIRY coverage, 25–40% ink: night, the fold wall in low tone, a clay oil lamp burning in a wall niche above the open gate gap, small warm-valued glow rendered as sparse dots; the flock a sleeping dotted bank in the lower corner; the Near One awake beside the niche, head raised at the flame. Somebody keeps the light on. Nobody asks who for.
subjects.strip-010-committee: MID coverage, 45–60% ink: seven sheep in a tight ring, heads inward, in the exact center of an otherwise empty pasture of quiet tone — unmistakably a meeting; behind them at great distance the tiny robed shepherd walks the ridge line away, crook over his shoulder, clearly getting on with it. The minutes will record that concerns were raised.
